title: Confidence Envelope Controller for Canary Evictions Based on Cost and Latency SLOs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Current canary eviction rules rely on fixed thresholds for latency and error-rate which cause noisy rollbacks during traffic spikes and token-cost fluctuations. We need a controller that reasons about uncertainty and cost to reduce false positives and to prioritize impactful evictions.

Goal: Implement a Confidence Envelope Controller (CEC) that computes dynamic, cohort-aware SLO envelopes (upper/lower bands) for latency, error rate, throughput, and token cost. The controller will trigger eviction decisions only when an externalized risk score derived from envelope breaches and cost exposure crosses an explainable policy threshold. The design should support canary, A/B, and shadow traffic modes and be pluggable into the rollout service.
acceptance_criteria: CEC produces per-cohort SLO envelopes (95%/99% bands) for latency, error-rate, throughput and token cost using 5m/30m sliding windows
Eviction decision is gated by a combined risk score that includes magnitude-of-breach, breach-duration, and cost-exposure and is configurable via rollout policy
False positive rate for canary evictions reduces by >= 30% on historical canaries (backtest on last 120 canaries), while maintaining detection of true regressions
Telemetry emitted for each decision: envelope metrics, risk_score, contributing_signals, and applied_action with trace_id
UI shows envelope bands and risk breakdown on the rollout detail page and allows manual override with explanation logged
Runbook updated and on-call playbook created with actionable steps for inspection and emergency rollback
tasks: Design: formalize envelope computation and risk score formula (stats + cost normalization)
Instrumentation: add per-route, per-cohort metrics for token-cost and throughput to rollout telemetry
Controller: implement CEC service with pluggable signal adapters (latency, error-rate, token-cost, throughput)
Policy: extend rollout policy schema to accept risk thresholds and hysteresis parameters
Backtest: run historical backtest harness across last 120 canaries and produce ROC/precision recall
UI: add envelope visualization and risk explanation in Console rollout page
Tests: unit/integration tests, simulated traffic e2e test against staging runtime
Docs: Confluence design doc and runbook, internal note to customers on rollout behavior change
decisions: Use hybrid statistical model: percentile-based envelopes for short windows (5m) and Bayesian shrinkage for longer windows (30m) to handle low-traffic cohorts
Normalize token-cost impact by converting token-cost delta into expected monthly spend delta per 1000 requests to make cost comparable to latency/error signals
Eviction gating requires both a risk_score > policy_threshold AND a minimum sustained breach duration to avoid flash evictions
Explainability requirement: store top-3 contributing signals for each decision and surface in Console
We will roll out CEC to low-traffic canaries first (<=5% traffic) and run for 2 weeks before enabling automatic evictions for medium traffic
